target_customer: Pharma partners and patients with tissue specific inflammatory disease, starting with inflammatory bowel disease; a drug developer that licenses or co develops a tissue targeting platform
problem: Non specific drugs cause toxicity and trial failures in tissue restricted inflammatory diseases. Eugit uses T cell receptors to steer therapies to diseased tissue.
business_model: Preclinical biotech platform (TAGHOME); no revenue, value comes from pipeline assets, partnerships and grants
product_category: Tissue targeted drug delivery using T cell receptors

founders.name: Nizar Batada
prior_employers: University of Edinburgh (tenure track group leader)
founders.background_notes: Source: YC company page and YC launch post.

founders.name: George Church
founders.background_notes: Named as co founder in the YC launch post and company site; the YC page lists only Batada as active founder. Education not stated in sources opened.

founders.name: Yoshi Fukazawa
education: Postdoc, Oregon Health and Science University

technical_complexity.rationale: Engineering T cell receptors as tissue homing delivery vehicles is research grade biology needing wet lab, preclinical models and eventually clinical trials; the company had 2 people at the YC page listing.

defensibility.rationale: Platform IP and the scientific pedigree of the founders could be protective if patents issue, but no patent or clinical data was found in sources opened.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent move found. No acquisition reported as of the sources opened.

market_need_then: The YC page cites 3.1 million US people with inflammatory bowel disease and toxicity of systemic drugs as the unmet need. The launch post cites checkpoint inhibitors and CAR T working for only a few cancers.

branding.domain_note: Uses eugittx.com (suffix tx for therapeutics), exact .com not found in sources.

brand_strength.rationale: No press or community material about the brand found; the draw is the George Church association, not the name.

pivots.from: Off the shelf gamma delta T cells for cancer immunotherapy (YC launch post)
pivots.to: TAGHOME tissue targeting of therapies, initially inflammatory bowel disease (current YC page)

outcome_analysis: Eugit is an active preclinical biotech with a very small team that shifted from cancer cell therapy at launch to tissue targeted delivery for inflammatory bowel disease. Public funding evidence is thin: an NSF SBIR Phase I grant in 2024 and an unverified YC amount. Founder pedigree from the Church lab is the main asset, while clinical proof is absent in the sources found.
notes: Unverified single aggregator figures: about $500K pre seed from YC in 2022-09 (VCBacked, LinkedIn page) and a $130K seed (Bounce Watch); not recorded as rounds. Nearby TCR companies found (GigaMune, Resseptor founded 2023) lacked dates near the batch, so competitor list is empty. Outcome and funding searches returned no primary press.
